columns.rationale: Two-letter IATA carrier code with null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 16 equal to row_count 16, so every row carries a unique, non-null code (samples: 9E, AA, DL, WN).
Full airline name with null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 16 matching row_count 16; samples such as 'Delta Air Lines Inc.' and 'JetBlue Airways' confirm clean text values.
Capture-tool record identifier flagged is_airbyte_metadata true; dropped as pipeline metadata with no business meaning.
Capture timestamp flagged is_airbyte_metadata true with a single distinct value 2026-09-02T23:26:17 across all 16 rows; dropped as pipeline metadata.
Capture metadata flagged is_airbyte_metadata true whose only distinct value is the empty object '{}'; dropped as pipeline metadata carrying no information.

decisions.rationale: carrier has distinct_count 16 equal to row_count 16 with null_rate 0.0, so the two-letter carrier code uniquely identifies each row and is declared as the grain.
duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across row_count 16, so no exact duplicate rows exist in bronze and no dedupe step is applied.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are all flagged is_airbyte_metadata true and are dropped; _airbyte_meta holds only '{}' and _airbyte_extracted_at a single load timestamp.

purpose: silver_airlines is a cleaned reference table mapping each two-letter IATA carrier code to its full airline name, covering the 16 carriers present in the bronze NYC airlines feed. It feeds joins from flight-level tables that carry only the carrier code.
usage: Join on carrier (the declared grain and primary key) to enrich flight records with the human-readable airline name. Both columns are non-null, so no null-handling is needed by consumers; treat name as display text, not a join key.
limitations: The table reflects a single bronze snapshot of 16 carriers; airlines not present in the source load are absent, and no historical name changes are tracked. No casts or renames were needed, and no duplicate handling was applied because duplicate_row_rate was 0.0.
